_comment: English Tier 0 rules. Editable: this is the list the user can change. Keys are matched case-insensitively on word boundaries.
_fillers_note: THREE lists, on two different axes. 'language_gated' ARE real words in other languages -- 'um' is Portuguese 'a/an' and German 'at/around', 'ah' and 'eh' are words elsewhere -- so they are only removed once the language is known to be this one. 'sentence_initial' are real words in THIS language, removed only when they open an utterance: deleting 'so' everywhere mangles 'so the thing is'. Cross-language gating is adopted from Handy's audio_toolkit/text.rs (MIT), which fails closed on unknown languages; the always/sentence_initial split was cross-checked against sebsto/wispr's FillerWordCleaner (Apache-2.0).
_punctuation_note: Spoken punctuation. Attached to the preceding word with no space.
_structure_note: Commands that break or classify blocks. Longest match wins, so 'new paragraph' is tried before 'new'.
_structure_in_list_only_note: Commands that are also ordinary words. 'bullet points' is a phrase people say; heard in real dictation on 2026-09-09, it turned the rest of the sentence into a list item. These only act while a list is open.
_structure_at_block_start_only_note: Commands that are also ordinary words: 'we are heading home', 'the title of the book'. Bare, they act only as the first words of a block that does not continue a sentence from the segment before; 'new heading' and 'new title' act anywhere.
_cadence_note: Spoken list cadence. 'one X two Y' becomes an ordered list only when three or more consecutive markers appear -- two is far too easy to trigger on ordinary speech about numbers.
_numbers_note: Conservative only. Standalone small numbers stay as words; digits are produced for quantities that read badly spelled out.
_stutter_note: A single repeated word is only a stutter for these. Repeating any other word is emphasis -- 'very very good' is not a stutter, and a length heuristic gets that wrong because 'very' is short. An explicit list is the only safe rule.
_phrases_note: Only unambiguous discourse markers, and only at the opening. Excluded deliberately: 'like I said' carries the information that the speaker is repeating themselves, and 'sort of'/'kind of' are hedges -- 'sort of working' is not 'working'. Those go to Tier 1, which has the context to judge.
